name: Knowledge Retention Backend V5.0
description: Backend state machine for guided knowledge-retention interviews over Dataverse and SharePoint

authFields.label: Client ID
authFields.description: Application (client) ID of the Azure app registration used for app-only access to Dataverse and Microsoft Graph.

authFields.label: Client secret
authFields.description: Client secret of the Azure app registration. Rotate before the configured expiry; expiry surfaces to interviewees as a contact-your-administrator error.

authFields.label: Dataverse environment URL
authFields.description: Base URL of the Dataverse environment, with no trailing slash (e.g. https://org12345.crm4.dynamics.com).

authFields.label: Knowledge prefill enabled
authFields.description: Set to true only once the delegated WorkIQ prefill (v1.1) is provisioned. While false, the consent step is skipped server-side, matching the original WorkIQEnabled=false behavior.

authFields.label: SharePoint site ID
authFields.description: Microsoft Graph site ID of the central CKR team site that stores interview folders. Format: host,siteCollectionId,webId.

authFields.label: Tenant ID
authFields.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID (GUID) of the BASF tenant that hosts the Dataverse environment and the CKR SharePoint site.

actions.name: Get runtime state
actions.description: Loads the caller's interview, topics, and questions and returns the computed next action plus a backend-authored instruction. Call once at the start of a conversation.

actions.name: Create interview
actions.description: Starts a new knowledge-retention interview for the caller in the chosen language. Refuses server-side if the caller already has an open interview.

inputFields.label: Interview language
inputFields.description: Language the interview is conducted in. The backend stores it and every later instruction is rendered in this language.

actions.name: Save discovery
actions.description: Saves the pre-interview discovery profile for the caller's open interview and advances it to the topic-generation stage.

inputFields.label: Business unit
inputFields.description: The employee's department, business unit, or team.

inputFields.label: Focus topics
inputFields.description: Topics the employee considers most important to capture before they leave.

inputFields.label: Responsibilities
inputFields.description: The employee's core responsibilities and recurring tasks, in their own words.

inputFields.label: Role
inputFields.description: The departing employee's role or job title.

inputFields.label: Tools and systems
inputFields.description: Tools, systems, and applications the employee works with day to day.

inputFields.label: KPIs and constraints
inputFields.description: Optional. KPIs the employee owns and any constraints or dependencies worth recording. Send only when the employee provides them.

actions.name: Save topics and questions
actions.description: Persists the generated interview topics and their questions for the caller's open interview, then advances it to the interview stage. Idempotent on retry.

inputFields.label: Topics
inputFields.description: The ordered list of interview topics, each with its ordered questions. Generate 4-6 topics with 3-6 questions each per the methodology skill.
inputFields.jsonSchema: {"type":"array","minItems":4,"maxItems":6,"items":{"type":"object","properties":{"order":{"type":"integer","description":"1-based topic order, most critical first"},"name":{"type":"string","description":"Topic name shown in bold to the interviewee"},"description":{"type":"string","description":"Optional one-line summary of what the topic covers"},"questions":{"type":"array","minItems":3,"maxItems":6,"items":{"type":"object","properties":{"order":{"type":"integer","description":"1-based question order within the topic"},"questionText":{"type":"string","description":"Verbatim question text, in the interview language, asked exactly as written"},"mandatory":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether the question must be answered (default true)"}},"required":["order","questionText"]}}},"required":["order","name","questions"]}}

actions.name: Set up interview folder
actions.description: Creates the SharePoint folder for the caller's interview on the central CKR site and grants edit access to the employee and their manager. Idempotent.

actions.name: Save consent
actions.description: Records the interviewee's explicit decision on knowledge prefill for the caller's open interview.

inputFields.label: Consent granted
inputFields.description: True only if the interviewee explicitly confirmed prefill. False if they declined. Never infer from a soft or implicit reply.

actions.name: Save answer
actions.description: Saves the interviewee's confirmed answer to the current question and returns the next state. Rejects the write with a conflict if the expected question order, or the expected topic order when supplied, no longer matches the backend.

inputFields.label: Expected question order
inputFields.description: The order number of the question the answer is for, taken verbatim from the last state. Used for optimistic concurrency; a mismatch returns a conflict and no write.

inputFields.label: Expected topic order
inputFields.description: The order number of the topic the question belongs to, taken verbatim from the last state. Question order restarts at 1 in every topic, so this stops a stale answer from landing on a same-numbered question in a later topic; a mismatch returns a conflict and no write.

inputFields.label: Final answer
inputFields.description: The interviewee's confirmed, final answer to the current question. It should capture the essence of the answer, and reassure the user a more extensive summary will be generated later. Do not over-summarize. Save only after explicit confirmation.

inputFields.label: Raw user messages
inputFields.description: Required. The interviewee's own messages for this question, in chronological order: the initial answer plus every follow-up, copied verbatim. Do not EVER paraphrase, condense, omit, or substitute the cleaned finalAnswer. This is of utmost importance.

actions.name: Save topic summary
actions.description: Saves the exact user-approved Markdown summary FILE for the current topic in Dataverse and advances the topic to completed. The agent must create or update it with the write document tool, attach or show that exact file, and get explicit approval before calling this action. This stores content only; it creates no Word file. Call generate_topic_document afterwards with the same topic order. Rejects the write with a conflict if the expected topic order no longer matches the backend.

inputFields.label: Expected topic order
inputFields.description: The order number of the topic the summary is for, taken verbatim from the last state. Used for optimistic concurrency; a mismatch returns a conflict and no write.

inputFields.label: Reviewed Markdown summary
inputFields.description: The exact Markdown file the user reviewed and approved. Attach the edited file after the user confirms it. The backend stores its full UTF-8 contents; do not replace it with a paraphrase or a different file.

actions.name: Generate topic document
actions.description: Creates the standardized Word document for one already-approved topic and files it in the caller's interview folder. The summary text is read from Dataverse, never from the caller, so save_topic_summary must have stored it first; pass only the topic order. Also ensures the Source transcripts/ and Supporting documents/ subfolders, files a Markdown source transcript under Source transcripts/, and lists the actual contents of Supporting documents/ in a closing section. Returns the .docx as a file attachment. Reruns best-effort replace the canonical generated .docx; if SharePoint cannot delete that existing file, the new document is filed with a deterministic -FINAL suffix. Reruns never touch user-supplied supporting files. Use this instead of building or uploading a topic .docx yourself.

inputFields.label: Topic order
inputFields.description: The order number of the topic whose document should be generated, taken verbatim from the last state (e.g. 2). Everything else — the summary text, file name, folder path, and interview — is resolved server-side. A topic without an approved stored summary is refused with a conflict and nothing is written.

actions.name: Upload document
actions.description: Uploads the final handover or a user-confirmed supporting file on the central CKR site. Final and legacy topic files are stored at the caller's interview-folder root; supporting files are stored in the fixed Supporting documents/ subfolder. The destination is resolved server-side from the caller's identity. Uploading with docType "final" also advances a finalized interview to Document Generated, which is what tells a later session the handover file was filed. Do NOT use this for per-topic documents: generate_topic_document produces those from the stored summary. If recovery reports a missing topic document, call generate_topic_document with its returned topic order. The docType "topic" contract remains only for backend legacy compatibility.

inputFields.label: Document type
inputFields.description: Whether this is the final interview summary, an optional supporting file, or a legacy per-topic document. Use "final" for the handover and "supporting" for a user-confirmed attachment. For per-topic documents, including recovery, call generate_topic_document with topicOrder instead; do not use "topic" in the agent flow. The "topic" value remains for backend legacy compatibility.

inputFields.label: File
inputFields.description: The single user-confirmed file to upload. The final document is a generated .docx; supporting files may use their original format.

inputFields.label: File name
inputFields.description: The unique file name to store, including its extension (e.g. Topic-1 Stakeholder map.docx, InterviewFinalSummary_42.docx, or Process-Checklist.pdf). Supporting files are stored under Supporting documents/; final and legacy topic files stay at the interview-folder root.

actions.name: Read supporting document
actions.description: Optional, read-only action for inspecting one previously uploaded and confirmed supporting file that is missing from chat. Call it only with the exact basename, including extension; the file name is resolved inside the server-owned Supporting documents folder for the caller's current or resumable completed interview. It cannot read other folders or arbitrary files and is not attached to the agent by default.

inputFields.label: Supporting file name
inputFields.description: The exact basename, including extension, of a previously uploaded and confirmed supporting file in this interview (for example, Process-Checklist.pdf). Do not provide a path or URL.

actions.name: Finalize interview
actions.description: Completes the caller's interview once every topic is summarized and every canonical Topic-n-{slug}.docx is present in the interview SharePoint folder (a previously uploaded Topic-n {topic name}.docx or deterministic -FINAL fallback also counts). If a topic file is missing, nothing is finalized; the missing file names and stored summaries are returned so those files can be uploaded first.

actions.name: Save feedback
actions.description: Saves the interviewee's three feedback answers on the most recently completed interview. Works after the interview is finalized.

inputFields.label: Helpfulness rating
inputFields.description: Answer to: how helpful was the agent in documenting your knowledge? A rating from 1 to 5, captured as text.

inputFields.label: Improvement feedback
inputFields.description: Answer to: what would you like to improve, which functionality did you miss? Free text.

inputFields.label: Intuitiveness rating
inputFields.description: Answer to: how intuitive was the agent to use? A rating from 1 to 5, captured as text.

actions.name: Revise answer
actions.description: Records a new version of the interviewee's answer to an EARLIER, already-answered question (not the question currently being asked). Requires finalAnswer plus rawUserMessages (verbatim revision transcript). The previous version is kept as history. If that question's topic summary was already approved, the summary is flagged for regeneration. Only works before the interview is finalized; identify the question by its topic and question order from the current state, never by an ID.

inputFields.label: Final answer
inputFields.description: The interviewee's confirmed corrected answer. Save only after explicit confirmation.

inputFields.label: Raw user messages
inputFields.description: Required. The interviewee's own messages for this revision, in chronological order: the correction plus every follow-up, copied verbatim. Do not EVER paraphrase, condense, omit, or substitute the cleaned finalAnswer. This is of utmost importance.

inputFields.label: Target question order
inputFields.description: The order number (from the current state) of the earlier, already-answered question being corrected. Pair it with topicOrder when that order exists in more than one topic.

inputFields.label: Expected answer version
inputFields.description: Optional. The latest known answer-version number for that question, used as a concurrency token. A mismatch returns a conflict and no write.

inputFields.label: Topic order
inputFields.description: Optional. The order number of the topic the question belongs to. Question order repeats across topics, so send this whenever the question order alone matches more than one answered question; a conflict response names the candidate topics.

actions.name: Get answers
actions.description: Reads back previously saved answers for the caller's open interview, optionally filtered by topic and/or question order. Includes the confirmed answer and rawUserMessages when stored. Read-only; use this to remind the interviewee what they answered, and as the primary source when building the final handover. Each question carries its answer version in `sequence`, which is what revise_answer's expectedSequence expects.

inputFields.label: Question order
inputFields.description: Optional. Limit results to this question, by its order number within its topic. Question order repeats across topics, so pair it with topicOrder when the topic is known.

inputFields.label: Topic order
inputFields.description: Optional. Limit results to this topic, by its order number from the current state. Required alongside questionOrder if the question order alone matches more than one topic.

actions.name: Admin: query records
actions.description: Runs an ad hoc query against any CKR Dataverse table with structured column filters, sorting, and projection. Field names, types, and valid operators are resolved live from Dataverse metadata, not hard-coded; call admin_describe_schema first (with the same table) to learn them rather than guessing. Unlike every other action here, this is NOT scoped to the caller's own interview: it is an admin/monitoring tool over the whole dataset, gated only by who has access to this connection. Returns matching rows as JSON by default, or as a downloadable CSV when exportAsCsv is set. An unknown table, field, or operator returns an error naming the problem and pointing back to admin_describe_schema.

inputFields.label: Table
inputFields.description: The CKR entity to query, by its Dataverse logical name or entity set name (e.g. ckr_interview / ckr_interviews). These names are effectively static, but call admin_describe_schema if unsure of the exact one for this environment.

inputFields.label: Columns to return
inputFields.description: Optional. Field identifiers (from admin_describe_schema) to include in each row. Defaults to every attribute on the entity when omitted.

inputFields.label: Export as CSV
inputFields.description: Return the matching rows as a downloadable CSV file instead of an inline JSON list.

inputFields.label: Filters
inputFields.description: Optional. Column filters to apply, ANDed together. Each entry needs a field (a field identifier returned by admin_describe_schema for this table, e.g. a lookup column reads as _ckr_interview_value), an operator, and a value. String fields support eq/ne/contains/startswith; numbers and dates support eq/ne/gt/ge/lt/le; booleans and GUIDs support eq/ne only.
inputFields.jsonSchema: {"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"field":{"type":"string","description":"Field identifier for the chosen table, from admin_describe_schema"},"operator":{"type":"string","enum":["eq","ne","gt","ge","lt","le","contains","startswith"]},"value":{"type":["string","number","boolean"]}},"required":["field","operator","value"]}}

inputFields.label: Max rows
inputFields.description: Optional. Maximum number of rows to return, capped at 5000. Defaults to 200.

inputFields.label: Sort by
inputFields.description: Optional. A field identifier (from admin_describe_schema) to sort by. Defaults to createdon.

inputFields.label: Sort direction
inputFields.description: Optional. Defaults to descending.

actions.name: Admin: describe schema
actions.description: Discovers the CKR Dataverse tables and columns that admin_query_records can filter, select, or sort by, resolved live from Dataverse's own EntityDefinitions/Attributes metadata rather than a hard-coded list, so it can't drift from what actually exists in this environment. Also resolves the human-readable labels for Choice/Picklist columns (e.g. ckr_topicstatus) where the environment supports it. Call with a table to get its columns, or omit table to list every ckr_ entity. Call this before admin_query_records if you don't already know the field names for a table.

inputFields.label: Table
inputFields.description: Optional. The CKR entity to describe, by its Dataverse logical name or entity set name (e.g. ckr_interview / ckr_interviews). Omit to list every entity whose logical name starts with ckr_.

actions.name: Get discovery profile
actions.description: Reads back the caller's saved pre-interview discovery profile (role, business unit, responsibilities, tools, focus topics, KPIs/constraints). Read-only; use this when building the final summary document, since finalize_interview's cover metadata only carries role and business unit.

actions.name: Abandon interview
actions.description: Cancels the caller's current in-progress interview. Use only when the interviewee explicitly wants to discard it; requires confirmation and cannot be undone. After success, do not start a new interview until they ask.
